text:
maya: Quick one — onboarding a Windows dev box and I keep getting 401s when I try to hit /v1/embeddings. I set REDWOOD_API_KEY in .env and copy it into GH Actions secrets. Using Basic because some infra tests expect Authorization header. Anyone seen Windows/GHA newline or quoting cause this?

chris: Windows CRLF + quoting is a classic. Also GH Actions secrets sometimes include a trailing newline if you copy with an editor. Can you print the raw length?

maya: how do I print raw length in PowerShell?

anika: PowerShell: `([System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($env:REDWOOD_API_KEY)).Length` should show if there's an extra byte for \r or \n.

maya: ok shows length 36 but expected 35. so extra char.

chris: if you're doing Basic, remember we encode `key:` (key followed by colon). If there's an extra newline you'll b64 encode that too and server rejects.

maya: in my script I used this in PowerShell: `$auth = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("$env:REDWOOD_API_KEY:`"))` — is that wrong?

anika: yeah that looks like you added an extra backtick/quote. For PowerShell safe base64: `'$b = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($env:REDWOOD_API_KEY + ":"))'` then `-Headers @{ Authorization = "Basic $b" }`. Avoid injecting extra quotes.

chris: alternative: use Bearer header instead: `Authorization: Bearer <key>` — less fiddly and our log redaction picks that up by default.

maya: concerned about proxy tests that assert Basic header format. Any patterns to normalize key between GH Actions and local dev?

anika: in GH Actions, when you set a secret via UI it usually is clean. But if you echo it in a runner with `echo "$SECRET"` you might add newlines. Use `printf '%s' "$SECRET" | wc -c` on linux to check. For Windows runners use the PowerShell length check. Also `trim()` in scripts helps: `($env:REDWOOD_API_KEY).Trim()`

ops-bot: note: redact service flags — we only auto-mask `Authorization: Bearer` tokens. Basic base64 may reveal API keys in logs if not masked.

maya: hmm ok, I can normalize with `.Trim()` and then encode. Is there a recommended canonical snippet for PowerShell -> Basic encoding?

dev-tools-bot: canonical snippet (internal): `# PowerShell
$raw = ($env:REDWOOD_API_KEY).Trim()
$pair = "$raw:`"   # key + colon
$b64 = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes($pair))
Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://api.redwood-inference.test/v1/embeddings" -Headers @{ Authorization = "Basic $b64" }`

anika: small extra: avoid using backtick to escape quotes inside the string; string concatenation with + or interpolation is clearer. Also check for invisible Unicode BOM if you edited .env in some editors.

maya: fixed it by trimming and switching to Bearer for local tests. I updated our onboarding .env example to avoid trailing quotes and added a PowerShell snippet in the quickstart. Will open a tiny PR.

chris: can you also add a short note in the infra playbook about redaction/Basic header? security might want to whitelist Basic patterns for redaction.

security: filed INFRA-4287 to review header redaction scope, linking your PR would help.

maya: thanks all — saved my afternoon :pray:
